topic: HCM LOS concept, service flow rate
idea: Service flow rate = max hourly rate sustainable at each LOS A-E (LOS F unpredictable); hourly rate defined as 4 x peak 15-min volume; design at LOS C/D. Report per element capacity, service flow rates for A-E and the service measure, with v/c kept as a secondary indicator that flags trouble even when LOS is acceptable.
does: For a road/junction returns the service flow rate boundaries per LOS and where the current demand sits, plus v/c.
outputs: service flow rate A-E, current LOS, v/c
notes: Pairs with SRC_010 road_los_report.

idea: Report a central value plus values for upward/downward assumptions on key inputs (especially +15% volume) so decisions rest on sensitivities, not a single LOS letter.
does: Re-runs or re-evaluates a result at -/+ X% demand and reports how delay/LOS change; one tool call yields a table.
outputs: KPI and LOS per factor
notes: A wrapper of existing tools; makes the assistant do it by default.

idea: Plot delay against cost for each alternative, drop dominated ones (costlier AND slower), compute slope = seconds of delay saved per dollar between alternatives and choose the cheapest that meets the target LOS.
does: Takes scenario results and unit costs, removes dominated options, ranks by delay saved per cost and flags those meeting a LOS target.
inputs: scenario KPIs, costs per scenario, LOS target
outputs: Pareto set, marginal slope, recommendation
notes: Costs would be supplied by the user.

topic: Lane count from demand and service flow rate
idea: Required lanes = demand flow rate / service flow rate per lane at target LOS (4,500/2,000 = 2.25 so 3 lanes); compare designs by LOS or by finding attributes for the target.
does: Gives minimum lanes per road or approach to hold target LOS from demand.
outputs: lanes needed
notes: Needs the service flow rates above.

idea: Show LOS for 15-min period by segment as a table with failing cells shaded (ordinal, not interval, so no averaging of letters); LOS F has no upper bound.
does: Returns a grid of LOS letters per segment per 15-min period from a run, marking cells worse than the objective.
outputs: grid and list of failing cells
notes: Pair with analyse_run output by time.

idea: PHF = V/(4*V15) (Eq 7-1, 7-2); peak flow rate v = V/PHF (7-3). A road with hourly volume below capacity still breaks down if the peak 15-min rate exceeds it; breakdown can last hours.
does: From a run's per-5s samples compute the hourly volume, peak 15-min flow rate, PHF per road and flag roads whose peak 15-min rate exceeds capacity though the hour does not.
outputs: PHF, peak 15 min rate, v/c on the peak 15 min
notes: Also a demand tool: convert hourly OD demand to the peak 15-min rate via a chosen PHF.

topic: Speed measures: space mean vs time mean
idea: Average travel speed = L / mean travel time (Eq 7-4, space mean, harmonic) never the arithmetic mean of spot speeds (time mean; example 40/60/80 km/h gives 60 vs 55.4); space mean < time mean, SR = 1.026 ST - 3.042.
does: Make KPIs report space-mean (distance over mean travel time) and check the existing mean speed definition; separate running speed and travel speed including stops.
outputs: travel speed, running speed, time mean speed
notes: Check results.py mean speed is vehicle-distance/vehicle-time.

idea: v = S x D (Eq 7-5); spacing = 1000/D (7-6); headway = spacing/speed (7-7); flow = 3600/headway (7-8). Speed-flow-density curve has free-flow speed Sf, optimum speed So, optimum (critical) density Do, jam density Dj, max flow vm; flow at any level occurs on an uncongested and a congested branch; LOS A-E on the uncongested side, F on the congested side.
does: Builds the speed-flow-density scatter and fitted capacity, critical density, jam density from a run's detector or lane samples, to validate the Krauss parameters against HCM-like capacity and to classify uncongested vs queued state.
outputs: capacity veh/h/ln, Do, Dj, Sf, speed at capacity, branch classification
notes: Calibration tool for the physics: compare simulated capacity with HCM base 2,200 pc/h/ln.

topic: Saturation headway and start-up lost time
idea: Saturation flow s = 3600/h (7-9), h taken from the 5th vehicle onward after a green start; start-up lost time l1 = sum of ti for first 4 vehicles (7-10); clearance lost time l2 = unused part of the change interval; lost time per movement per hour = cycles x (l1+l2).
does: Measures saturation headway, start-up lost time and clearance lost time from stop-line departure times after each green in a run; reports against HCM defaults (s 1900/h/ln, l1 2.0 s).
outputs: h, s, l1, l2 with n cycles
existing: partial: not_built notes start-up loss 1.8 vs 2.0 s only
notes: Directly tests signal physics; gives data for optimise_signals lost time.

idea: Queue clearing time tQ = s r/(s - v) (7-11); max queue QM = v r/3600 (7-12); mean while present QQ = v r/7200 (7-13); mean queue Q = QM tQ/(2C) (7-14); oversaturated queue length QL = T(v - c)/(N ds) (7-15).
does: Quick analytical queue length per signal approach to compare against measured queue lengths in a run and size storage lanes (spillback).
inputs: arrival rate, saturation flow, red, cycle, lanes
outputs: max queue veh, queue duration, queue length m
notes: Gives spillback check: queue vs road length.

topic: Design hour from daily demand (K and D factors)
idea: Directional design-hour volume DDHV = AADT x K x D (Eq 8-1); K typically 0.09-0.10 (Exhibit 8-9), D up to 0.65 on radial routes; AADT = AWDT/1.07 (8-2); design to the 30th-100th highest hour (knee of the ranked-hour curve); test LOS for higher hours; PHF 0.80-0.98 in urban areas.
does: Given a daily OD demand and the daily curve, derive the peak hour K (from the curve), the directional split D per road pair, the DDHV and the PHF-adjusted 15-min flow, and warn when the design hour is not the busiest.
inputs: daily demand per pair, daily curve
outputs: K, D, DDHV, peak 15-min rate
notes: K and D can be computed exactly from the simulated daily profile rather than assumed.

idea: Observed lane distribution: heavy vehicles concentrate in right (shoulder) lanes (e.g. combinations 88.5% in lane 1), shoulder lane carries less total traffic; volume split by lane depends on regulations, access points and OD.
does: Behaviour rule and a check: report the share of each vehicle type per lane in a run and compare to the typical keep-right pattern for trucks and buses.
outputs: per-lane type shares
notes: Could also seed lane selection for heavy types in LC2013 strategic changes.

topic: HCM reference values to validate the physics
idea: Reference benchmarks: freeway base capacity 2,400 pc/h/ln (FFS 120) and 2,300 (FFS 110), observed max lane volumes 2,000-2,650 veh/h/ln; signal saturation flow 1,900 pc/h/ln (headway 1.9 s; studies 1,470-2,000), start-up lost time 1.0-2.0 s, saturation headway established from 6th-7th queued vehicle; speed barely changes with flow until about 1,600 veh/h/ln; green over 40-50 s is less efficient; two-lane highway 2,800+ both ways observed in Europe; arterial per-lane flow = volume/(g/C).
does: One check that simulates a standard lane/stop line and compares measured capacity, saturation headway, start-up lost time and speed-flow knee with these HCM ranges, pass/fail per metric.
outputs: measured vs reference range per metric
existing: partial: check_calibration (demand counts), not_built notes on start-up loss
notes: A validation suite complements the unit tests; the reference ranges give pass bands.

idea: Real streams show few headways under 1.0 s (platoons, minimum near 1 s; 0.5 s would mean 7.5-9 m gaps at 95 km/h); shoulder lane has more dispersed headways and a lower flow than inner lanes.
does: Histogram of time headways per lane from detectors, reports share under 1 s and mean; flags unrealistic tails (Krauss tau too small) and platoon proportion.
outputs: headway histogram, % under 1 s, mean, CV
notes: Pairs with the fundamental diagram; Poisson shift models exist in the cited ref 14.

idea: Observed bus capacity: with intermediate stops rarely above 120 buses/h per lane, 180-200 with two lanes or passing; downtown streets with 2-3 boarding positions 80-100 buses/h (5,000-7,500 pax/h); commuter berths 8-10 buses per berth per hour, intercity 1-2; typical 14 m bus 43 seats + 37 standees, 18 m articulated 65 + 55; pax per bus 35-55.
does: Compares simulated bus headway/throughput on a bus stop or corridor against these ceilings and warns when a configured headway cannot be served (stop berth saturation).
outputs: buses/h per stop vs benchmark, berth utilisation
notes: Feeds TSP studies.

topic: Minimum sample size for a mean
idea: n >= 4 s^2 / xi^2 (A9-1), s^2 sample variance (A9-2), gives the observations needed so the mean's margin of error xi holds at about 90-95% confidence; for small n replace 4 with 2t (t Student). Example: s=45, xi=5 needs 324 observations, not 15.
does: After a few seeds, tells how many more runs are needed for a target margin of error on any KPI (a power/precision planner).
inputs: KPI values per seed, target error (abs or %)
outputs: n needed, seeds still to run
existing: partial: run_experiment reports replications for a precision; not_built: power analysis
cite: Ch 9 App A, Eq A9-1, A9-2
notes: Source gives the exact z=2 formula and the t-correction for n<5.

idea: Algorithm to back-solve the maximum volume per LOS: fix non-volume inputs by facility/area type and lane count; for each LOS threshold find Vol1 below and Vol2 above (doubling) then bisect on the LOS measure until the bracket is small; if even low volume exceeds the LOS A threshold then A is unachievable; report to nearest 10/50/100.
does: Implements the search used by service_volume_table with a headless run or analytic model as the LOS function.
outputs: max volume per LOS A-E
notes: With the simulator as the LOS function each probe is a run; use noise-aware stopping.

idea: Inputs are accurate to only 5-10%; small differences between alternatives are not necessarily real; a value just under a LOS threshold has a probability of exceeding it; report to 2-3 significant digits (v/c 2 dp, delay 1 dp, speed 1 dp).
does: For a KPI against a LOS threshold, report the probability (from seed variance) that the true value crosses it and tag differences as not significant.
outputs: P(exceed), significance flag, rounded values
notes: Reporting rule for the assistant.

topic: Facility aggregation by segment and point
idea: Facility = segments (uniform demand/capacity, directional) joined at points (junctions); estimate segment and point travel time/delay, convert to person-hours, sum to facility, corridor and area.
does: Chain per-road running time plus per-junction control delay along an ordered path into a route/corridor total (person-hours).
outputs: travel time split into segment and point delay, person-h
notes: Uses vehicle occupancy for person-delay.

topic: Urban street class and LOS by speed ratio
idea: Classify an arterial into class I-IV from function (principal/minor) and design category (high-speed 75-90 km/h, 0.3-1.2 signals/km; suburban 65-75, 0.6-3; intermediate 50-65, 2-6; urban 40-55, 4-8); default FFS I 80, II 65, III 55, IV 45 km/h and signal density 0.5/2/4/6 per km. LOS is by average through travel speed, about 90% (A), 70% (B), 50% (C), 40% (D), 33% (E) of FFS; FFS measured midblock at flow below 200 veh/h/ln with signals ignored; study length at least 1.5 km downtown, 3 km elsewhere, shorter treated as intersections.
does: Classifies each corridor of connected roads, computes free-flow speed (signals green) vs travel speed from a run and returns arterial LOS A-F with the speed ratio.
outputs: street class, FFS, travel speed, LOS, signals/km
cite: Ch 10 II, Exhibits 10-3 to 10-6, LOS text; Ch 15 Exhibit 15-2
notes: Cut-offs per class are in ch 15 (read later); here only the ratio guide.

idea: LOS criteria were developed for 15-min periods; if v/c > 1 use multiple consecutive 15-min periods carrying residual queue forward (Ch 16 App F) or a longer period with a modified PHF; do not average LOS letters across periods.
does: Reports LOS and residual queue per consecutive 15-min window of a run for each approach, carrying overflow, rather than one average.
outputs: per-15-min delay, v/c, residual queue, LOS
cite: Ch 10 II Length of Analysis Period
notes: Pairs with los_time_segment_grid.

idea: Effective green g = G + Y - l1 - l2, lost time tL = l1 + l2, extension e about 2 s (part of change interval used) and start-up lost l1 about 2 s so for typical conditions effective green = actual green plus yellow/all-red minus 2 s (Eq 10-1 typical).
does: Reports measured effective green, lost time and green extension per phase from stop-line crossing times, to feed Webster/optimise_signals lost time.
outputs: effective green, e, l1, l2 per cycle
notes: Same measurement as measure_saturation_flow.

topic: Signalised intersection LOS by control delay
idea: LOS from average control delay per vehicle for a 15-min period: A <=10 s, B 10-20, C 20-35, D 35-55, E 55-80, F >80; LOS F can occur with v/c < 1 (long cycle, poor progression) and a saturated group can have low delay, so report both v/c and delay; cycle failure = a green that does not clear its queue (overflow).
does: Per signal approach/lane group from a run: mean control delay (vs uncontrolled travel time), v/c, share of cycles that failed (queue not cleared), LOS A-F.
outputs: delay s/veh, LOS, v/c, cycle failure %, stops per vehicle
existing: none (not_built: per-junction KPIs and level of service)
cite: Ch 10 III Level of Service; Ch 16 Exhibit 16-2
notes: Control delay = delay relative to free travel without the signal, includes deceleration and acceleration.

topic: Turning movements from leg volumes (matrix balancing)
idea: Estimate an intersection turning O-D matrix from entering and exiting leg volumes: Tij = Ti Tj / sum_i Tj (10-4) with U-turns zero; then iterative proportional fitting: Rj = Tj/sum_i Tij (10-5), scale columns, Ri = Ti/sum_j Tij (10-6), scale rows, stop when diffs (10-7, 10-8) under 10 veh/h or iteration limit. Defaults when unknown: 10% left, 10% right.
does: Gets turn flows at every junction from counted approach and exit volumes (end flows or detector counts) by IPF, for check_calibration and signal timing inputs.
outputs: turn matrix per junction, closure error
existing: partial: calibrate_demand (OD from counts on roads)
cite: Ch 10 III Turning Movement Estimation, Eq 10-4 to 10-8
notes: Pure stdlib; cheap diagnostic for what turn split a signal plan should assume.

idea: Forecast control type from two-way peak-hour volumes on major and minor streets: signal at high volumes, all-way stop in the middle band, two-way stop at low minor volume; minor > major is infeasible; roundabout may fit in the same ranges.
does: For each junction suggests signal / roundabout / stop control from its approach volumes and compares with the current control, flagging mismatches.
outputs: recommended control, margin, flags
notes: Chart boundaries are plot-only; refine with the 8-h MUTCD warrants or ch 17 capacity.

topic: Turn lane and lane count rules of thumb
idea: Exclusive left lane probably needed at 100 veh/h left (double at 300); exclusive right lane when right > 300 veh/h and adjacent mainline > 300 veh/h/ln; add lanes so through+right(+left) <= 450 veh/h/ln; assume 3.6 m lanes; defaults: lost time per cycle 16/12/8 s for 4/3/2 phases, cycle 70 s CBD and 100 s other, PHF 0.92, base saturation flow 1900 pc/h/ln.
does: Design check listing approaches whose turn volumes warrant a turn lane or whose per-lane volume exceeds 450 veh/h/ln.
outputs: warranted additions, flagged approaches
notes: Storage bay length method in ch 16 App G.

idea: Consider protected left phase if more than one left lane, left demand over 240 veh/h, or cross product of left-turn volume and opposing through volume exceeds 50,000 (1 opposing lane), 90,000 (2) or 110,000 (3+); split phase allowed if opposing approaches offset by over 20 m or both single-lane protected lefts.
does: Flags signalised approaches that should use a protected left phase and the phase count/lost time that implies (L 8/12/16 s).
inputs: junction left and opposing through volumes, lanes
outputs: protected recommended or not, product, margin
cite: Ch 10 III Lost Time and Estimation of Signal Phasing
notes: ACMS drives on left or right and has 2/4 phase signals; use as an analyse_network warning.

idea: Six arrival types for progression quality (1 very poor to 6 exceptional) by signal spacing (under 500 m, 500-1000 m, 1000 m+ isolated) and coordination; progression factor PF 1.00 for type 3, 0.84 for type 4 at g/C 0.45; arrival type refined from the share of vehicles arriving on green; upstream filtering factor I 0.92-0.09 if the upstream signal is within 1 km.
does: Measures per approach the proportion of vehicles arriving on green and maps it to the HCM arrival type and progression quality, to judge offsets from TRANSYT/Synchro.
outputs: P (arrival on green), arrival type 1-6, platoon ratio Rp
cite: Ch 10 III Arrival Type, Exhibit 10-18; Ch 15 Exhibit 15-4
notes: Direct test of coordination; arrival on green is easy to measure at the stop line.

topic: Pedestrian-driven minimum cycle and weighted green
idea: Minimum pedestrian clearance 3 s per through lane + 3 s for a left lane + 6 s walk; minimum cycle 60/70/80 s for 1/2/3-lane approaches; weighted g/C for a street = average of the critical intersection through g/C and the mean of the others (default 0.45).
does: Lower bound on cycle and green from crossing width so optimise_signals/Webster never gives an unwalkable plan.
outputs: minimum green per phase, minimum cycle
notes: ACMS has pedestrian crossings (describe lists crossings).

idea: Share of traffic in the most heavily used lane: 2 lanes 52.5% (fLU 0.952), 3 lanes 36.7% (0.908); exclusive left 1 lane 1.000, 2 lanes 51.5% (0.971); exclusive right 2 lanes 56.5% (0.885); factor nearer 1 as demand nears capacity; wide lanes over 6 m may act as two.
does: Reports measured lane share per approach from a run and compares with HCM fLU, to detect under-used lanes (blocked by lane choice or turn bays).
outputs: share by lane, fLU

topic: TWSC priority ranks and gap effects
idea: Two-way stop priority hierarchy: rank 1 major through/right; rank 2 major left and minor right (yield to major through only); rank 3 minor through; rank 4 minor left (yields to all). Capacity of controlled legs depends on gap distribution, critical gap and follow-up time; effects: two-stage gap acceptance with median or TWLTL raises capacity, platoons from a signal within 0.4 km raise minor capacity, pedestrian blockages (count groups) impede lower ranks, flared approach allows two vehicles at stop line, shared lanes limit use of gaps; preemption of major streams when congested.
does: Checks that give-way junction behaviour follows the four ranks, and reports observed minor-street waiting times against the rank (to find a stalled rank 4 left turn).
outputs: delay per rank, queue, wait time
cite: Ch 10 IV Flow at TWSC, Gap Acceptance Models, Capacity of TWSC
notes: Two-stage crossing at medians is a candidate feature (not built: impatience).

idea: AWSC operates in two- or four-phase rotation; saturation headway grows with conflicting presence: Case 1 only subject approach, 2 plus opposing, 3 plus conflicting, 4 two others, 5 all approaches; single-lane approach saturation 1,100 veh/h alone, 2,000 veh/h with four evenly loaded approaches; LOS from control delay; adding turn pockets barely helps.
does: Reference for a stop-sign rotation rule and measurement of departure headway by case count for an all-way stop in the simulation.
outputs: saturation headway per case
cite: Ch 10 IV Characteristics of AWSC, Exhibit 10-25, 10-30

topic: Left-turn lane warrant on two-lane roads
idea: Minimum approach volume for a left-turn lane on a two-lane highway at an unsignalised junction by opposing volume, percent left turns and speed (e.g. 60 km/h, 800 opposing, 5% left: 330? see table) from AASHTO.
does: Flags junctions on two-lane roads that should have a left-turn pocket.
inputs: approach volume, opposing volume, left %, speed
outputs: pocket needed boolean
notes: Table needs careful reading from the PDF; lower value.

topic: Quick estimation of signal critical v/c
idea: Planning method: lane volumes (RT factor 0.85 single/shared, 0.75 double; LT 0.95 single, 0.92 double; sneakers remove 2 veh/cycle of protected-plus-permitted lefts, floor 4/cycle); critical phase volume CV per phase plan (6 plans, lost time 4 s per phase); critical sum CS = sum CV; reference sum RS = 1710 x PHF x fa (fa 0.90 CBD); cycle C = L/(1 - min(CS,RS)/RS) (A10-1) within min (60 s for pedestrians) and max (150 s); green g = (C-L) CV/CS (A10-2); critical v/c Xcm = CS/(RS(1 - L/C)) (A10-3); status: <=0.85 under, 0.85-0.95 near, 0.95-1.0 at, >1 over capacity (Exhibit A10-9); then lane-group delay d = d1 PF + d2 + d3.
does: Per signalised junction gives the critical volume-to-capacity ratio and under/near/at/over-capacity status for the current plan and a recommended cycle and splits, as a quick analytical check before running a simulation.
inputs: junction turn flows, lanes, phasing, lost time, PHF
outputs: CS, Xcm, status, cycle, greens per phase
existing: partial: set_signal_timing/optimise_signals (Webster, TRANSYT, Synchro); no critical v/c status
cite: Ch 10 Appendix A, Eq A10-1 to A10-3, Exhibits A10-4 to A10-9
notes: Sums critical lane volumes; ACMS already knows its phases; compare with Webster's C0 = (1.5L+5)/(1-Y).

idea: Left-turn equivalence EL1 and shared-lane adjustment fDL: multi-lane fDL = [(N-1)+exp(-N VL EL1/600)]/N with a minimum using VL*Cmax/3600; single-lane fDL = exp(-0.02(EL1+10 PLT) VL Cmax/3600); protected-plus-permitted fDL = 1/(1+PLT(235+0.435 Vo)/(1400-Vo)) for Vo<1220 else 1/(1+4.525 PLT); sneaker capacity 7200/C vehicles/h; EL1 >3.5 means left capacity comes from sneakers so protect it.
does: Estimate how much a permitted left turn in a shared lane reduces through capacity, and flag junctions where lefts rely on sneakers.
inputs: left volume, opposing volume, lanes, cycle
outputs: fDL, EL1, sneakers per cycle, protect flag
notes: Ties to the protected left warrant idea.

idea: Pedestrian flow v = S x D (11-1) or v = S/M with space M m2/p; capacity about 75 p/min/m (4,500 p/h/m) at 0.8 m/s and 0.4-0.9 m2/p; walkway LOS by space A >5.6, B 3.7-5.6, C 2.2-3.7, D 1.4-2.2, E 0.75-1.4, F <=0.75 m2/p (flow 16/23/33/49/75 p/min/m); queuing area LOS by space A >1.2, B 0.9-1.2, C 0.6-0.9, D 0.3-0.6, E 0.2-0.3; platoon flow is one LOS level worse than average; walking speed 1.2 m/s (1.0 if over 20% elderly, 1.5 free-flow sidewalks), start-up time 3 s; body ellipse 0.5 x 0.6 m, 0.75 m2 buffer.
does: For a crosswalk corner or sidewalk of known effective width and pedestrian demand (institutions' walkers), compute space per pedestrian, LOS and signal-driven platoon peaks.
inputs: width, pedestrian flow, signal cycle, speed mix
outputs: space m2/p, LOS, platoon flow, queue area LOS
existing: none (not_built: pedestrians; institutions have a Walk mode)
notes: ACMS has Walk share from institutions but no pedestrian model; this gives a static analysis without simulation.

idea: Uninterrupted bike path LOS by hindrance (share of path where a cyclist is affected by meeting/passing events): A <=10%, B 10-20, C 20-40, D 40-70, E 70-100, F 100; surrogate is events/h (passes and meetings) which rises past capacity; LOS F at flows far below capacity (1,600 bikes/h/ln two-way, 3,200 one-way; 2,000 saturation interrupted); three effective lanes (3.0 m) much better than two (2.4 m); defaults speed 25 km/h, PHF 0.80, width 2.4 m. Interrupted lanes use control delay like vehicles.
does: Counts passing and meeting events per cyclist on a bike lane from a run and grades LOS; for design suggests 2.4 vs 3.0 m width.
inputs: bike volume, direction split, ped volume, effective lanes
outputs: events/h, hindrance, LOS
existing: none (Bike is a vehicle type; no lane-level bike model)
notes: Only meaningful if bikes get separate lanes in ACMS.

topic: Pedestrian platoon size at unsignalised crossing
idea: Typical crossing platoon Nc = (vp e^{vp tc} + v e^{-v tc})... of vp (ped flow), v (veh flow), tc (critical gap) (Eq 11-3); start-up times 1.8-2.6 s median, 3.7-4.0 s 85th percentile; crosswalk width default 3.6 m, corner radius 7.3 m (13 m with trucks).
does: Sizes the pedestrian blockage and waiting for a zebra crossing from the vehicle flow and critical gap, and the delay vehicles see.
inputs: vehicle flow, pedestrian flow, critical gap
outputs: platoon size, vehicle blockage probability
notes: Equation garbled in text extraction; refer to the PDF.

idea: Platoon quality KPI for two-lane/rural roads: percent time spent following = share of travel time behind a slower vehicle, surrogated by the percentage of vehicles with headway under 3 s at a point; with average travel speed defines LOS (class I both, class II PTSF only).
does: Computes share of vehicles (or time) in headways under 3 s per road from detectors/trajectories; flags platooning where overtaking is impossible (single lane).
outputs: PTSF %, mean speed, class LOS
notes: Cheap from headway histogram; applicable also to bus platoons.

idea: Multilane FFS = base 100 km/h minus adjustments: lane width below 3.6 m, lateral clearance below 3.6 m total, undivided median -3 km/h, each 6 access points/km (one side) -4 km/h; speed flat below 1,400 pc/h/ln, then drops 12 km/h to capacity 2,200 pc/h/ln (FFS 100); recreational drivers up to 20% lower capacity; enforcement effect decays exponentially downstream (13-15 km, 2-3 days after).
does: Suggest a posted/target speed for a road from its access-point density, lane width and median, and warn when a user's speed setting is inconsistent with the access density.
inputs: road lane width, access/junction density, median
outputs: estimated FFS, adjustments
notes: Access density = junctions per km on one side (ACMS has all junctions).

topic: Two-lane highway LOS and passing lanes
idea: Two-lane roads: LOS A-E by percent time spent following (A <=35%, B 50, C 65, D 80, E >80; class II 40/55/70/85) and average speed; total two-way capacity 3,200 pc/h, service flows 490/780/1190/1830 pc/h two-way base; opposing flow reduces speed; no-passing zones 20/50/80% by terrain; optimal passing lane length 0.8 km at 100 pc/h up to 1.6-3.2 km at 700 pc/h; defaults split 60/40 (80/20 recreational).
does: Grades rural two-lane road segments by PTSF and suggests passing-lane length where platooning is high.
outputs: PTSF, speed, LOS, suggested passing lane length
notes: ACMS roads are lane-based; passing on two-lane roads is not simulated, so low value.

idea: Three flow types on a freeway segment: undersaturated (unaffected by bottlenecks), queue discharge (flow just past a bottleneck, 2,000-2,300 pc/h/ln, accelerating back to FFS in 1-2 km, about 5% lower than the pre-breakdown maximum), and oversaturated (stop-and-go queues, not standing). Bottlenecks arise from merges, weaves, lane drops, incidents (even shoulder incidents).
does: For a bottleneck in a run, measures the maximum pre-breakdown flow, the queue discharge rate after breakdown and the drop percentage, and classifies each lane-time cell into the three regimes (using speed and density).
outputs: max flow, discharge flow, drop %, regime time shares, queue extent
notes: Validates Krauss breakdown behaviour; the 5% drop and 1-2 km recovery are targets.

idea: Weaving segment = merge followed closely by diverge (or on-ramp and off-ramp joined by an auxiliary lane); weaving flows A-D and B-C cross, nonweaving A-C, B-D. Type A: every weaving vehicle makes one lane change across the crown line (ramp-weave); Type B: one weaving movement needs no lane change, the other at most one (lane balance at exit gore: lanes leaving diverge = lanes approaching + 1); Type C: one movement needs 2+ lane changes. Weaving vehicles confined to the lanes next to the crown line. Mandatory lane changes must fit in the weave length; discretionary ones need not.
does: Classifies each weaving section of a built interchange or consecutive ramps (A/B/C), checks lane balance at diverges and reports lane-change need per weaving vehicle vs available length.
outputs: weave type, lane changes per vehicle, lane balance flag, length
existing: partial: build_interchange builds ramps; no weave analysis
notes: Pair with ch 24 procedure when read.

idea: Base FFS 120 km/h rural, 100 urban (default 110); reduce for lane width, right lateral clearance (shoulder lane affected below 1.8 m, median lane below 0.6 m), fewer lanes (2 lanes lower FFS), interchange density above 0.5/km (spacing under 2 km; ideal 3 km, minimum 1 km); FFS is the mean car speed below 1,300 pc/h/ln, not the posted limit nor the 85th percentile; default PHF 0.95 congested.
does: Compares speed settings of freeway roads to the expected FFS from lanes and interchange spacing and flags suspect limits.
outputs: expected FFS, mismatch

topic: Ramp junction capacity and influence area
idea: Merge/diverge influence area is lanes 1 and 2 plus the ramp lane for 450 m downstream of a merge / upstream of a diverge; merge capacity = capacity of the downstream basic segment (turbulence does not reduce it) with at most 4,600 pc/h entering lanes 1+2 plus ramp; diverge capacity = min(upstream mainline, downstream mainline + ramp) with at most 4,400 pc/h in lanes 1+2; most diverge breakdowns come from the off-ramp lacking capacity (queue spills onto the mainline); ramp over 1,500 veh/h needs 2 lanes; defaults acceleration lane 180 m, deceleration 42 m, ramp FFS 55 km/h; short accel lanes force stopping and mainline disruption; ramp-street queues can back to the freeway.
does: For every ramp of an interchange: computes merge/diverge capacity limits, 450 m influence-area density from a run, flags short acceleration lanes, ramps needing a second lane and off-ramps whose queue reaches the mainline.
inputs: interchange ramps, mainline lanes, demand or run_id
outputs: capacity constraints, lane 1-2 flow, density, spillback length, flags
notes: ACMS has trumpet/diamond/SPUI; this evaluates them (ramp terminals in ch 25/26).

idea: Required lane changes per hour: Type A 2 per weaving vehicle (1,000 x 2 flows = 2,000/h), Type B 1,000/h, Type C at least 2,000/h; weaving vehicles occupy at most Nw(max) lanes: 1.4 (A), 3.5 (B), 3.0 (C); if Nw > Nw(max) operation is constrained (weavers worse, non-weavers better); procedure valid to 750 m; shorter length raises lane-change intensity; length measured from 0.6 m to 3.7 m gore spacing.
does: Tells whether a weaving section is constrained and how many forced lane changes per metre it requires; compare against measured lane changes in a run.
outputs: lane changes/h, Nw, Nw(max), constrained flag
notes: Pairs with interchange_weave_check; needs Nw model from ch 24.

idea: Summarise a facility with time-space contour maps (speed, density, v/c where 1.00 marks bottlenecks and >0.90 near capacity, and congestion status); congested region area = distance-hours of congestion (horizontal extent = length, vertical = duration); aggregate vehicle-km, vehicle-h and person-h per 15-min interval, per segment and overall; cumulative distributions of speed/density.
does: Builds a segment x 15-min matrix of speed, density and v/c from a run, finds bottleneck cells (v/c about 1) and computes congested km-h, queue extent and duration; returns as table/heatmap data.
outputs: matrices, congested distance-hours, bottleneck list, VKT, VHT, person-h
notes: Generalises los_time_segment_grid; one KPI (congested km-h) comparable across scenarios.

idea: Evaluate management strategies as base case vs alternative with different demand/capacity: incident management (over 50% of freeway congestion is incident-caused; early detection, quick clearance), lane control signals, ramp closure/metering (entry control), HOV lanes and HOV bypass, traveller information, congestion pricing, work-zone and special-event plans; demand shifts in time, route, mode or elimination.
does: Experiment template: inject a lane-closing incident at a time/place and compare clearance strategies (response time, lane control, ramp metering on upstream ramps) against the no-management base using paired seeds.
outputs: delay, queue length, recovery time per strategy with paired tests
existing: partial: schedule_emergency, run_experiment, build_scenario (no incident/ramp metering)
notes: Ramp metering and incidents are not in ACMS; extension candidates.

topic: TSP decision rules and net person delay
idea: Active bus priority only at intersections below capacity (so LOS does not worsen); conditional priority only when the bus is behind schedule (AVL); evaluate the net change in person delay for all users (bus passengers vs motorists, bicyclists, cross-street buses) before granting; passive vs active; treatments: green extension, early start, special bus phase, phase suppression, unconditional vs conditional preemption; cross-street buses may lose more than the favoured route gains; risk to coordinated progression.
does: Gives the TSP agent a number to decide with: expected person-seconds saved (bus load x time saved) minus person-seconds lost on conflicting approaches (queue x extra red x occupancy), plus the junction v/c and bus lateness as gating conditions; also logged as an explanation of each decision.
inputs: bus load, schedule adherence, junction queues, v/c, treatment
outputs: net person-delay change, grant/deny with reason
existing: partial: TSP extension decided by LLM agent (no explicit person-delay or v/c gating)
cite: Ch 14 II Bus Priority Treatments, Person-Delay Considerations, Exhibits 14-15, 14-16
notes: Fits ACMS people-carried KPI and vehicle occupancy; also usable to judge DEVL on person terms.

topic: Bus loading area and stop capacity
idea: Loading area capacity falls with dwell time and rises with g/C: 15 s dwell 63 bus/h at g/C 0.5, 100 at 1.0; 60 s 26/36; 120 s 15/20 (15 s clearance, 25% queue failure rate, CV of dwell 60%); linear berths lose efficiency (1-5 berths at 60 s, g/C 1.0: 36, 67, 89, 96, 98); sawtooth/drive-through berths 100% effective; nearside stops worst, farside best; off-line stops add re-entry delay; skip-stop with platoons about +67% bus lane capacity; busway person capacity = bus/h x load x PHF; dwell time = boardings x service time + door time; person capacity at maximum load point.
does: Computes bus/h and person/h capacity of each bus stop from dwell time, signal g/C, berths and failure rate, and flags stops where timetable headways exceed it (queueing buses block traffic).
inputs: stop, headway, dwell time, g/C, berths
outputs: capacity bus/h, utilisation, queue probability
existing: none (not_built: passengers at bus stops, boarding times)
notes: Full capacity formula is in ch 27 (to read).

topic: Transit availability and quality of service framework
idea: Transit availability = spatial (stop within 400 m / 5 min walk of origin AND destination; 800 m for rail), temporal (service at the needed time), information; then comfort and convenience: four service measures: frequency (stop), hours of service (route segment), passenger load factor (seats occupied; 1.0 all seats, inner city up to 2.0), reliability (on-time and headway regularity); system measures: service coverage (% of area with at least hourly service), transit/auto travel time difference, % person-minutes served. Late bus picks up more passengers and falls further behind (bunching), following buses run early and light.
does: Reports for the bus network: share of institutions' people (catchment) within 400 m of a stop, frequency per stop, headway regularity (coefficient of variation of observed headways, bunching events), load factor, and transit vs car travel time per OD pair.
outputs: coverage %, frequency, headway CV, bunching count, transit/auto time ratio
existing: partial: list_institutions, add_bus_stop (no coverage or reliability metrics)
notes: Headway CV is cheap from bus stop arrival times in a run; supports TSP evaluation (does priority reduce bunching).

idea: Control delay d = d1 PF + d2 + d3 (15-1); uniform delay d1 = 0.5 C (1-g/C)^2 / (1 - min(1,X) g/C) (15-2, first Webster term, X capped at 1); incremental delay d2 = 900 T [(X-1) + sqrt((X-1)^2 + 8 k I X/(c T))] (15-3) valid for all X, T analysis period h, c lane group capacity, k actuated adjustment (0.5 pretimed, 0.04-0.5 actuated), I upstream filtering (1.0 isolated); d3 initial queue delay (Ch 16 App F); progression PF = (1-P) fPA/(1-g/C); platoon ratio Rp = P C/g (15-4, 15-5).
does: Predicts per-approach control delay analytically (v/c, g/C, cycle, T=0.25 h) and compares it with the simulated delay from a run to validate signal physics and to screen signal plans without simulating.
inputs: cycle, effective green, saturation flow, flow, T, arrival type
outputs: d1, d2, d3, total delay, LOS, predicted vs simulated gap
existing: partial: optimise_signals uses Webster; no HCM delay model or comparison with a run
notes: Short closed-form; use as expected value to test the Krauss/signal simulation.

idea: Urban street LOS by average travel speed (km/h): class I (FFS 90-70) A >72, B 56-72, C 40-56, D 32-40, E 26-32; class II (70-55) A >59, B 46-59, C 33-46, D 26-33, E 21-26; class III (55-50) A >50, B 39-50, C 28-39, D 22-28, E 17-22; class IV (55-40) A >41, B 32-41, C 23-32, D 18-23, E 14-18; F below. Travel time = running time per km (Exhibit 15-3 by segment length, class, FFS) plus through control delay at each signal; segment lengths under 400 m use 400 m; method not valid for turns above 20% or when queues spill upstream.
does: Gives the LOS cut-offs for the arterial_los tool and the running time per km table.
outputs: LOS letter
notes: Adds the numeric thresholds missing from the Ch 10 idea.

topic: Arterial travel speed and speed-flow sweep
idea: Segment/section travel speed S = 3600 L / (TR + d) (15-6) with TR total running time (s) and d control delay of through movements (plus midblock delays); street through capacity c = N s g/C (15-7) at the critical (highest through v/c) intersection; speed-flow curves vs peak-direction v/c for signal densities (e.g. class III 2/3/4 signals/km, 120 s cycle, g/C 0.45, s 1,700) show speed drops with signal density and arrival type (type 1 to 6 changes mean speed by roughly -3 to +8 km/h); upgrading class can lower LOS because expectations rise.
does: Runs the same corridor at several demand scales and reports travel speed against the critical through v/c, with the analytic expected curve for comparison; reports which intersection is critical.
inputs: corridor path, demand scale list, seeds
outputs: speed vs v/c table, critical intersection, knee point
notes: A canned experiment template.

idea: Upstream signals reduce arrival variance: I = 1 - 0.91 Xu^2.68 (Xu <= 1; 1.0 isolated 1.6 km or more from the nearest signal); actuated incremental delay factor k = (1-2kmin)(X-0.5) + kmin by unit extension (kmin 0.04 at 2 s to 0.23 at 5 s), 0.5 at X >= 1; platoon ratio default Rp 0.333/0.667/1.0/1.333/1.667/2.0 by arrival type; PF table by g/C and arrival type (AT3 = 1.0).
does: Parameter set for analytic_signal_delay and for an actuated-signal extension's expected benefit.
outputs: I, k, PF
notes: Needed only if the analytic delay model is built.

idea: s = s0 N fw fHV fg fp fbb fa fLU fLT fRT fLpb fRpb (16-4), s0 = 1,900 pc/h/ln: lane width fw = 1 + (W-3.6)/9 (W >= 2.4 m); heavy vehicles fHV = 100/(100 + %HV (ET-1)), ET = 2.0; grade fg = 1 - %G/200 (-6 to +10); parking fp = (N - 0.1 - 18 Nm/3600)/N (each maneuver blocks 18 s, Nm <= 180/h, within 75 m of stop line, >= 0.05); local buses fbb = (N - 14.4 NB/3600)/N (14.4 s per stop, NB <= 250/h, >= 0.05); area fa = 0.90 CBD; lane utilisation fLU = vg/(vg1 N) (16-5); left turns exclusive protected 0.95, shared fLT = 1/(1+0.05 PLT); right turns exclusive 0.85, shared 1 - 0.15 PRT, single 1 - 0.135 PRT; ped-bike fLpb, fRpb.
does: Predicts a lane group's expected saturation flow from geometry and mix (lane width, trucks, grade, bus stops, turns) and compares it with the saturation flow measured in the simulation, to show which factor the simulated drivers under- or over-react to; also makes capacity PCU-aware.
inputs: lane width, heavy %, grade, bus stops, turn shares, lanes
outputs: s in veh/h, factor breakdown, vs measured s
notes: Fills the not-built PCU item; ACMS vehicle types have PCU (stored).

topic: Critical lane group path and Xc
idea: Capacity ci = si gi/C (16-6); degree of saturation Xi = vi C/(si gi) (16-7); intersection critical v/c Xc = sum(v/s)ci x C/(C-L) (16-8); critical path through the cycle: exactly one critical lane group moving at all times (excluding lost times), maximum sum of v/s over overlapping leading/lagging and protected+permitted phases; lost time tL applied each time a critical movement starts (continuing movements not re-charged), L = n tL; a low cycle gives a high Xc so Xc alone is misleading; Xc below 1 means all movements fit by proportional green allocation.
does: Finds the critical path and sum of critical v/s for the junction's phase plan, then Xc and the minimum cycle C = L/(1 - sum(v/s)) for stability; used to explain why a plan fails and to check optimise_signals results.
inputs: junction phases, lane group flows and saturation flows, lost time
outputs: critical path, sum v/s, Xc, minimum cycle
cite: Ch 16 II, Eq 16-6 to 16-8, Exhibits 16-8 to 16-10
notes: ACMS has 2 or 4 phases; the critical path concept still helps for lead/lag later.

idea: Minimum green for a pedestrian phase Gp = 3.2 + L/Sp + 0.81 Nped/WE (WE > 3.0 m) or 3.2 + L/Sp + 0.27 Nped (WE <= 3.0 m) (16-2), L crosswalk length, Sp 1.2 m/s (15th percentile speed), 3.2 s start-up, WE effective crosswalk width; also analysis period T extended to cover the period of oversaturation, multi-period analysis when carry-over exists.
does: Lower bound for each signal phase so crossings stay walkable; the signal tools reject plans below it.
inputs: crossing length, width, pedestrians per cycle
outputs: minimum green
notes: Replaces the rougher 3 s/lane rule from Ch 10 App.

topic: Signal diagnosis from delay versus v/c
idea: Interpretation rules: acceptable intersection delay but bad lane group means re-split green/phase plan; high delay with low v/c means cycle too long or inefficient phases; high delay and high v/c is critical (delay explodes with small demand changes, consider geometry and signal redesign); critical v/c > 1 means capacity is insufficient (longer cycle, new phase plan, more lanes); LOS F can happen at v/c < 1 and LOS better than E at v/c > 1; compare delay by lane group, because an intersection average can fall when volume rises on low-delay movements; use arrival (demand) volumes, not departure counts, when v/c > 1.
does: Per signalised junction returns a ranked list of causes (long cycle, bad split, over capacity, poor progression, queue spillback) from delay, v/c and critical v/c, with a suggested fix, for the LLM to explain and act on.
outputs: diagnosis class, evidence numbers, suggested change
notes: Deterministic rule table; makes explanations consistent.

idea: When v/c exceeds 1.0 departures are below arrivals: capacity checks must use arrival demand (the demand generated/entering the queue), not the counted departures, otherwise v/c is underestimated; a future forecast is an arrival volume.
does: For each approach compares vehicles generated/arrived at the stop line with those discharged and flags approaches where the discharge is capacity-limited, so v/c is computed from arrivals.
outputs: arrivals, departures, queue growth, true v/c
notes: Matters for check_calibration which compares counts.

idea: Permitted left turn lane groups have a minimum capacity of (1 + PL) x 3600/C (sneakers: about one or two vehicles per cycle) regardless of opposing flow; the protected-plus-permitted uniform delay uses a queue accumulation polygon with six cases by Xperm and Xprot (Exhibit 16-23).
does: Sets a floor of the left-turn capacity in analytic checks and a rule for the simulation's sneaker behaviour at the end of green.
outputs: minimum capacity veh/h

topic: Control delay from queue count samples
idea: Control delay per vehicle by sampled in-queue counts: time-in-queue = Is x (sum Viq / Vtot) x 0.9 (A16-1) with Is the count interval (10-20 s, not a divisor of the cycle), plus an acceleration/deceleration correction = fraction stopping x CF (CF +2 to +9 s by free-flow speed and vehicles stopping per lane per cycle, Exhibit A16-2); counting must continue until every vehicle that arrived in the period has exited; oversaturated sites use the input-output technique (arrivals minus departures) or zoned surveys; a queue-join rule: within one car length of a stopped vehicle.
does: Computes control delay for each signal approach from the existing 5-s results samples (queue counts) when per-vehicle trip times are not stored, with the 0.9 sampling factor and accel/decel correction, and by input-output for oversaturated cases.
inputs: 5-s queue counts per approach, arrivals, free-flow speed, cycle
outputs: control delay s/veh, fraction stopping
existing: partial: not_built lists exact per-vehicle trip times within 5 s sample
cite: Ch 16 App A, Eq A16-1, Exhibits A16-1, A16-2
notes: In the simulator exact stop-line crossings and stops are known, so exact control delay = actual minus free-flow travel time is simpler; use these formulas to compare with the sampled version.

idea: Use simple two-phase control unless turns need protection (more phases raise lost time share); multiphase options: exclusive left phase (efficient when opposing lefts are near equal), leading/lagging green when unequal or one left only, four-phase when both streets need lefts; protected lefts also when opposing speed > 65 km/h; dual-ring concurrent phasing (barrier) for actuated; controllers pretimed, semi-actuated (major street nonactuated and coordinated, minor actuated), fully actuated (isolated, variable cycle).
does: Suggests 2-phase, exclusive-left, lead/lag or 4-phase for each signalised junction from turn volumes and opposing speed, and flags junctions where the current plan wastes lost time.
inputs: junction turn volumes, opposing speed, lanes
outputs: recommended phase plan, lost time per cycle
cite: Ch 16 App B, Exhibits B16-1, B16-2
notes: Pairs with left_turn_phase_check.

idea: Fully/semi-actuated phase logic with per-phase settings: minimum initial interval, maximum initial, added initial per actuation, unit extension / minimum allowable gap (2-3 s), gap reduction rate (linear), maximum green MxG, intergreen Y, pedestrian Walk+FDW minimum, recall mode (none, min, max, ped, coord), minimum phase time MnV = initial + MnA + Y; detector length and setback, presence mode (gap = headway minus detector occupancy t0 = 3.6(Ld + Lv)/SA, vehicle length 5.5 m); phase skipped without demand; dual-ring concurrent phasing with barrier, independent termination of first phases (overlap), leading/lagging via phase reversal; sneakers 2 per cycle and free queue behind a left-turner.
does: Adds gap-out actuated control (min/max green, unit extension, recall, skip) to the signal agent so ACMS can compare pretimed, SCATS/SCOOT and actuated plans and give the TSP agent green-extension actions.
inputs: detector length/setback, extension, min and max green, recall, intergreen
outputs: phase durations per cycle, cycle length, skipped phases
existing: none (not_built: actuated signals; SCATS tactical control)
notes: Placeholder rule: System 1 beyond the signal agent stays placeholder; actuated control is deterministic rules.

idea: Average actuated phase time = start-up lost + queue service time gs + green extension time ge + intergreen: gs = fq qr r/(s - qg) with fq = 1.08 - 0.1 (G/MxG)^2 (B16-8); ge = (e^{lambda(e0 + t0 - Delta)} - 1)/(phi q lambda) - 1/lambda... with bunched-exponential headways (B16-9 to B16-12: phi = exp(-b Delta q), lambda = phi q/(1 - Delta q), Delta 1.5 s and b 0.6 single lane; 0.5/0.5 two lanes; 0.5/0.8 three or more); iterate cycle until green deficiency under 0.1 s (example: 675 veh/h two-phase converges to 37.7 s phase, cycle 75.4 s; unit extension 2 s gives 65.6 s).
does: Predicts the average cycle and splits an actuated controller will run for a given demand, to set expectations and test the actuated controller implementation.
inputs: arrival rates, saturation flow, controller settings, detector length
outputs: expected phase times, cycle length, convergence trace
cite: Ch 16 App B, Eq B16-8 to B16-12, Exhibit B16-6
notes: Fixed-point iteration, stdlib.

topic: Actuated controller setting rules and experiment
idea: Findings from ten actuated-control alternatives: near capacity gap-out alone distributes green badly (a phase hitting max green starves others, delay 47 s vs 23 s with maxima at 100% of design splits), so maxima must be set (100-150% of design green) to apportion time; at 70% volume the same settings work (delay 10 s) and cycle varies 62-77 s with unit extension; unit extension must exceed departure headway by 50% (2 s min; 3 s for 2 s headway); coordinated semi-actuated: coordinated phase on recall max, give unused green to the coordinated phase (half the cycle difference per iteration); adjusted minimum phase time AVM = MnV (1 - e^{-qC}) when phases are skipped.
does: Experiment template for the assistant: run pretimed vs actuated (with several max-green rules and unit extensions) at 100% and 70% demand with paired seeds and report delay, cycle length and starved phases.
outputs: delay, cycle, v/c per phase for each setting
cite: Ch 16 App B, Exhibits B16-14 to B16-16, Eq B16-13, B16-14
notes: Depends on actuated_signal_control.

idea: Permitted left capacity by gap acceptance: filter saturation flow sLT = voe e^(-voe tc/3600) / (1 - e^(-voe tf/3600)) with critical gap tc = 4.5 s, follow-up tf = 2.5 s exclusive lane or 4.5 s shared lane, voe the effective opposing flow (veh/h/ln); through-car equivalent EL1 = sHT/sLT (exclusive) or sHT/sLT - 1 (shared), table 1.3-4.0 for opposing flow 1-1200; green split into gq (opposing queue clearing; gq = 4.943 volc^0.762 qro^1.061 - tL single lane), gf (shared lane unblocked before the first left arrives, gf = G e^(-0.860 LTC^0.629) - tL) and gu (filtering); fm = gf/g + gu/g/(1 + PL(EL1-1)); shared multilane fLT = (fm + 0.91(N-1))/N; sneakers (1 + PL) per cycle, minimum fm 2(1+PL)/g; opposing queue ratio qro = 1 - Rpo go/C.
does: Analytic reference for how many left turns a permitted phase should pass given opposing flow, to test and tune the gap acceptance parameters in the simulation (critical gap, follow-up time) and detect unrealistic blocking of left turns.
inputs: opposing flow, cycle, green, left share, lanes
outputs: expected left capacity per cycle vs simulated
cite: Ch 16 App C, Eq C16-1 to C16-7, Exhibit C16-3
notes: The tc/tf formula (Harders/Siegloch) also governs ch 17 unsignalised capacity.

topic: Pedestrian and bicycle blockage of turns
idea: Turning capacity reduced by conflicting crossing flow: pedestrian flow while green vpedg = vped C/gp; pedestrian occupancy OCCpedg = vpedg/2000 (<= 1000) or 0.4 + vpedg/10,000; bicycle occupancy OCCbic = 0.02 + vbicg/2700; combined OCCr = OCCped + OCCbic - OCCped OCCbic; for permitted lefts the opposing queue consumes pedestrian green gq/gp and the gap probability e^{-5 vo/3600}; unblocked share ApbT = 1 - OCCr (receiving lanes = turn lanes) or 1 - 0.6 OCCr; factor fRpb = 1 - PRT(1 - ApbT)(1 - PRTA).
does: Quantifies how many turns per cycle are lost to pedestrian and cyclist crossings at each junction (from institutions' walkers and crosswalks) and tests whether simulated turn capacity is reduced as expected.
inputs: pedestrian and bicycle volumes, cycle, green, turn share
outputs: conflict occupancy, turn capacity factor
cite: Ch 16 App D, Eq D16-1 to D16-8
notes: Only if a pedestrian model is added.

topic: Back of queue and queue storage ratio
idea: Average back of queue per lane Q = Q1 + Q2 (G16-6): Q1 = (vL C/3600)(1 - g/C) PF2 / (1 - min(1,XL) g/C) (G16-7) with PF2 = (1 - Rp g/C)(1 - vL/sL)/((1 - g/C)(1 - Rp vL/sL)) (G16-8); Q2 = 0.25 cL T [(XL - 1) + sqrt((XL-1)^2 + 8 kB XL/(cL T) + 16 kB QbL/(cL T)^2)] (G16-9) with kB = 0.12 I (sL g/3600)^0.7 pretimed or 0.10 I (...)^0.6 actuated; percentile queue Q% = Q fB%, fB% = p1 + p2 e^(-Q/p3) (70th: 1.2, 0.1, 5; 85th 1.4, 0.3, 5; 90th 1.5, 0.5, 5; 95th 1.6, 1.0, 5; 98th 1.7, 1.5, 5 pretimed); queue storage ratio RQ = Lh Q/La (Lh average spacing, La available storage); RQ >= 1 means blockage; initial queue added to flow vL = v + Qb/T.
does: For each signalised approach (and turn bay) predicts mean and 95th percentile back of queue in metres, compares with road/bay length (spillback test) and with the maximum queue measured in a run; flags approaches that will block upstream junctions or turn bays.
inputs: flows, saturation flow, g/C, cycle, T, lane lengths, queue spacing (about 7 m per vehicle)
outputs: mean and percentile queue, storage ratio, spillback flag
existing: none (analyse_network flags short roads only; not_built: queue per junction)
cite: Ch 16 App G, Eq G16-6 to G16-14, Exhibits G16-5, G16-6
notes: Percentile queues are cheap from the run: record queue length per cycle and take percentiles directly; use the formula for pre-run screening.

idea: Direct measurement of prevailing saturation flow: record stop-line crossing time of each queued vehicle's front axle; saturation flow starts at the 4th vehicle (10-14 s into green) and ends with the last queued vehicle; headway = (t_last - t_4)/(n - 4); s = 3600/headway; at least 15 cycles with more than 8 queued vehicles; note heavy and turning vehicles, pedestrians and bus blockage.
does: Protocol details for the measure_saturation_flow tool: use only headways after the 4th vehicle, at least 15 cycles with more than 8 vehicles in the queue, separate through-car only base value (1,900 pc/h/ln).
outputs: s per lane, n cycles
notes: Adds sample-size and reference-point rules to the earlier idea.

idea: Two-way stop capacity: conflicting flow vc,x per movement from the priority ranks (e.g. minor right vc,9 = v2/N + 0.5 v3 + v14 + v15; minor through includes 2 x major lefts; minor left includes all major flows plus half of minor opposing through/right); critical gap tc,x = tc,base + tc,HV PHV + tc,G G - tc,T - t3,LT (17-1), base tc (two-lane major): major left 4.1, minor right 6.2, minor through 6.5, minor left 7.1 s (four-lane 4.1/6.9/6.5/7.5), heavy vehicles +1.0 (2.0 four-lane), grade +0.1/+0.2 per unit; follow-up tf,x = tf,base + tf,HV PHV (17-2), base 2.2, 3.3, 4.0, 3.5 s; potential capacity cp,x = vc,x e^{-vc tc/3600} / (1 - e^{-vc tf/3600}) (17-3); impedance: Rank 2 cm = cp; Rank 3 cm = cp x prod p0,j with p0,j = 1 - vj/cm,j (17-5 to 17-7); Rank 4 uses p' = 0.65p'' - p''/(p''+3) + 0.6 sqrt(p'') (17-8, p'' = p0,j p0,k), cm,l = p' p0,j cp,l (17-9, 17-10); LOS by control delay A 0-10, B 10-15, C 15-25, D 25-35, E 35-50, F >50 s (Exhibit 17-2).
does: Analytic capacity and delay of each give-way/stop movement at a junction from major flows, to validate the simulated gap acceptance (Krauss/SUMO junction model) and to say which minor movement starves; also gives LOS per minor movement.
inputs: junction movement flows, lanes, heavy %, grade
outputs: conflicting flow, tc, tf, potential and movement capacity, delay, LOS per movement
existing: partial: roundabout capacity measured on simulated drivers only; not_built: critical gap estimation, impatience
cite: Ch 17 Part A, Eq 17-1 to 17-10, Exhibits 17-2, 17-4, 17-5
notes: Comparing simulated minor-street throughput against cp,x is a strong physics validation.

topic: Upstream signal platoon blocking of minor streets
idea: A signal within 0.4 km on the major street makes gaps non-random: four flow regimes (no platoon, platoon from left, from right, both) and during a dense platoon (headway below critical gap) minor streams cannot enter; queue discharge time gq = gq1 + gq2 (17-18 to 17-20) with P = Rp geff/C; dispersion alpha 0.35-0.55 by median and lanes, beta = 1/(1+alpha), F = 1/(1 + alpha beta ta), ta = D/Sprog; maximum platooned flow vc,max = sf[1 - (1-F)gq...] (17-21), minimum 1,000 N veh/h; blocked proportion p = (tp,T + tp,L)/C; unconstrained if pdom + psubo/2 <= 1; unblocked proportion per minor movement (Exhibit 17-16); capacity cplat = px cr,x with conflicting flow during unblocked period vc,u = (vc - s(1-p))/p (17-28, 17-29).
does: For a stop/give-way junction close to a signal, computes the share of time the minor movements are blocked by platoons and the resulting capacity loss, and checks that simulated minor-road waiting matches (and explains why moving a signal offset helps a minor road).
inputs: upstream signal cycle, green, spacing, speed, flows
outputs: blocked proportion per movement, platoon capacity
cite: Ch 17 Part A, Eq 17-17 to 17-29, Exhibits 17-10 to 17-16
notes: Links coordinated signal offsets with minor-street access.

topic: Two-stage crossing and flared approach capacity
idea: Median storage for m vehicles allows two-stage gap acceptance: a = 1 - 0.32 e^{-1.3 m}, y = (cI - cm,x)/(cII - vL - cm,x), cT = y^{m+1}... capacity combining stage I and II capacities (17-30 to 17-33), extra critical gap adjustment +1.0 per stage?; flared minor approach: capacity interpolates between shared-lane cSH and separate-lane sum csep by storage n up to nMax = max round(Qsep + 1): cact = ((sum csep - cSH)/nMax) n + cSH (17-36); shared lane capacity cSH = sum vy / sum(vy/cm,y) (17-15); pedestrian blockage fpb = v w/(Sp 3600) with Sp 1.2 m/s (17-11); 95th percentile minor queue Q95 = 900T[(vx/cm - 1) + sqrt((vx/cm - 1)^2 + (3600/cm)(vx/cm)/(150T))] (cm/3600) (17-37), mean queue = delay x flow/3600.
does: Capacity gain from a median refuge or flare for minor crossings, and the 95th percentile queue on each minor approach, so the assistant can recommend median islands and storage lengths at stop-controlled junctions.
inputs: movement capacities, median storage, flare spaces
outputs: two-stage capacity, flared capacity, Q95
notes: Q95 formula alone is cheap and generic (any queue with capacity cm and flow vx).

idea: Unsignalised control delay d = 3600/cm,x + 900 T [ (vx/cm,x - 1) + sqrt((vx/cm,x - 1)^2 + (3600/cm,x)(vx/cm,x)/(450 T)) ] + 5 (17-38), T = 0.25 h, the 5 s covers deceleration and acceleration; valid below saturation; 4 vehicle-hours/h of delay equals a mean queue of 4; control delay in the field = time from stopping at the end of queue to departing the stop line, including deceleration to queue speed.
does: Expected delay of each minor movement from flow and capacity, to compare with simulated delay and check calibration of give-way behaviour.
outputs: expected control delay and mean queue
notes: Companion to unsignalised_capacity.

topic: Control type warrants and shared-lane delay
idea: All-way stop warrants (MUTCD): interim before a signal, 5+ accidents in 12 months, or total entering volume at least 500 veh/h for any 8 h plus minor-street vehicle+pedestrian at least 200/h with 30 s average delay in the peak hour (70% of the volume if the 85th percentile major speed exceeds 65 km/h); 11 signal warrants; LOS F at a stop junction does not imply the signal warrant is met (random arrival assumption, minor left capacity ~85 veh/h at 50 s); judge with v/c, queue and 95th percentile queue, not only delay of the worst movement; delay to Rank 1 vehicles from a shared major left lane dRank1 = (1 - p0*) dM,LT (17-39); separate left lane lowers total delay though the left movement alone looks worse.
does: Checks stop-vs-signal decisions for a junction against the volume warrants (8-h volumes from the daily curve) and reports multiple measures (v/c, queue, delay) rather than a single LOS.
inputs: junction approach volumes by hour (daily demand), speeds, delay
outputs: warrant met flags, margin, measures
cite: Ch 17 Part A, Interpreting Results, Determining Intersection Control Type
notes: Uses ACMS's 24-hour demand profile; MUTCD thresholds.

idea: AWSC capacity by iteration: degree of utilisation x = v hd/3600 per approach/lane; five degree-of-conflict cases C1..C5 (none, opposing only, one conflicting, ...) with probabilities from the other approaches' x (17-47 to 17-51); departure headway hd = sum P(Ci) hsi (17-52), service time ts = hd - m (move-up 2.0 s, 2.3 s for groups 5-6), repeat until hd changes < 0.1 s, initial hd 3.2 s; base saturation headways 3.9-4.5 s (case 1) to 9.6-13.3 s (case 5) by geometry group, adjustments LT +0.2/0.5, RT -0.6/-0.7, HV +1.7 s; capacity = flow at which x reaches 1; delay d = ts + 900T[(x-1) + sqrt((x-1)^2 + hd x/(450T))] + 5 (17-55); LOS as TWSC; two-phase vs four-phase rotation; one-way crossings s = 2 s1[1 + lambda_o (s2 - s1)]/(1 - lambda_N lambda_W (s2 - s1)).
does: Analytic capacity and delay for an all-way stop from approach flows by the iterative headway model; reference for any all-way stop control added to the simulation and for comparing against stop-controlled junctions.
inputs: approach lane flows, geometry group, heavy %, turning shares
outputs: departure headway, capacity, delay, LOS per approach
cite: Ch 17 Part B, Eq 17-42 to 17-69, Exhibits 17-26 to 17-35
notes: Only useful if all-way stop control is offered in ACMS (set_junction_control types).

idea: Single-lane roundabout entry capacity ca = vc e^{-vc tc/3600} / (1 - e^{-vc tf/3600}) (17-70), with bounds: upper tc 4.1 s, tf 2.6 s; lower tc 4.6 s, tf 3.1 s; vc = circulating flow in front of the entry (e.g. entry 7, 8, 9 faces v1 + v2 + v10, include U-turns; exiting traffic ignored); valid for vc under 1,200 veh/h; approach v/c = va/ca; multilane capacity less than proportional; left-turn paths around the island reduce capacity (longer intraplatoon headways).
does: For each roundabout entry gives the HCM2000 expected capacity band for the actual circulating flow and checks whether the capacity measured on the simulated drivers falls inside; also reports v/c per entry.
inputs: entry flows, circulating flow per entry from the turn matrix
outputs: capacity lower/upper, v/c, measured vs band
existing: partial: describe (roundabout design NCHRP 672), Roundabouts row: entry capacity measured on simulated drivers; not_built: roundabout capacity per approach in the Summary
notes: Circulating flow derivation from OD turn flows is the useful new piece.

idea: Signalised crosswalk average pedestrian delay dp = 0.5 (C - g)^2 / C (18-5), g = Walk + first 4 s of flashing Don't Walk; LOS A < 10 s, B 10-20, C 20-30, D 30-40, E 40-60, F >= 60 with rising noncompliance risk beyond 30 s; unsignalised crossing: critical gap tc = L/Sp + ts (18-17, Sp 1.2-1.5 m/s), group gap tG = tc + 2(Np - 1) with spatial distribution Np = INT[0.75(Nc - 1)/WE] + 1 (18-18, 18-20), delay dp = (e^{v tG} - v tG - 1)/v (18-21), LOS A <5 s, B 5-10, C 10-20, D 20-30, E 30-45, F >45; crossing time t = 3.2 + L/Sp + 0.81 Nped/WE (18-13); street-corner time-space TS = C (Wa Wb - 0.215 R^2) (18-6), holding Qt = v R^2/(2C) (18-7), circulation space M = TSc/(4 vtot) (18-10); walking speed along an urban street SA = LT/(sum Li/Si + sum dj) (18-22) with LOS A > 1.33 m/s ... F < 0.58; shared path events F = Fp + 0.5 Fm with Fp = Qsb(1 - Sp/Sb), Fm = Qob(1 + Sp/Sb) (18-3, 18-4).
does: Computes pedestrian delay and LOS at each crossing from the signal plan (or traffic flow for unsignalised), and the corner space per pedestrian; lets the assistant weigh pedestrian delay against vehicle delay when changing signals.
inputs: crossing length/width, cycle, pedestrian green, pedestrian flow, vehicle flow
outputs: mean pedestrian delay, LOS, noncompliance risk, corner space
notes: Closed form; only needs signal timings, so no pedestrian simulation required.

idea: Off-street bike path events: Fp = 0.188 vs (19-1), Fm = 2 vo (19-2), F = 0.5 Fm + Fp (19-3) for N(18 km/h, 3 km/h) speeds; shared path with pedestrians Fp = 3 vps + 0.188 vbs, Fm = 5 vpo + 2 vbo (19-5, 19-6), F = vp(2.5 + 0.5p) + vb(1 - 0.812p) (19-8); general events = 2 flow sigma/(sqrt(pi) mean speed) (Exhibit 19-3); LOS events/h two-lane 2.4 m: A <=40, B 60, C 100, D 150, E 195; three-lane 3.0 m: 90/140/210/300/375; signal bike lane capacity cb = 2,000 g/C (19-9) (base up to 2,600), control delay uses uniform term only (19-10) (cyclists leave the route instead of queueing); LOS delay A <10 ... F >60; bike travel speed LOS A >22, B 15-22, C 11-15, D 8-11, E 7-8 km/h; running speed 25 km/h on arterials.
does: Equations behind bike_event_los plus signalised bike-lane capacity and delay for the Bike type's travel on roads.
inputs: bike flows by direction, speeds, g/C
outputs: events/h, capacity, delay, LOS

topic: Two-lane highway speed and PTSF equations
idea: Two-way segment: ATS = FFS - 0.0125 vp - fnp (20-5) with FFS = BFFS - fLS - fA (20-2, lane/shoulder width up to -10.3 km/h, about 0.4 km/h per access point/km), PTSF = BPTSF + fd/np (20-6), BPTSF = 100(1 - e^(-0.000879 vp)) (20-7), capacity 1,700 pc/h per direction and 3,200 both directions (tunnels/bridges 3,200-3,400); vp = V/(PHF fG fHV); no-passing zones and directional split corrections; facility totals vehicle-km VKT = 0.25 V Lt and travel time TT = VKT/ATS; FFS from field speed SFM + 0.0125 Vf fHV (20-1) when measured above 200 pc/h; FFS measured with at least 100 vehicles.
does: Closed-form speed and PTSF for rural two-lane segments to complete the two_lane_los tool.
outputs: ATS, PTSF, LOS class I/II
notes: Low priority: ACMS does not model passing on the opposing lane.

topic: Reference speed-flow curves and density LOS
idea: Multilane/freeway reference: speed equals FFS up to 1,400 pc/h/ln then S = FFS - (c1 - c2/...)((vp - 1400)/(a FFS - b))^1.31 (e.g. FFS 90-100: S = FFS - (FFS - 630/25... )), capacities 2,200/2,100/2,000/1,900 pc/h/ln at FFS 100/90/80/70; LOS by density A 7, B 11, C 16, D 22, E 25-28 pc/km/ln (v/c A 0.32, B 0.50, C 0.72, D 0.92, E 1.00 at FFS 100; service flow 700/1100/1575/2015/2200); FFS = BFFS - fLW - fLC - fM - fA (21-1), lane width 3.0 m -10.6 km/h, 3.3 m -3.1, total lateral clearance, undivided -2.6?, access points; speed limit +11 km/h (65-70) or +8 km/h (80-90) gives base FFS; density D = vp/S.
does: A reference curve with LOS density bands that fundamental_diagram and benchmark_physics compare the simulated lane against, and a unit for density-based LOS.
outputs: reference speed, density, LOS band, capacity
notes: Exact curve coefficients in Exhibit 21-3 text.

idea: Capacity adjustments for scenario tests: incident capacity available by lanes and blockage (2-lane direction: shoulder disablement 0.95, accident 0.81, one lane blocked 0.35, two blocked 0; 3 lanes 0.99/0.83/0.49/0.17; 4 lanes 0.99/0.85/0.58/0.25/0.13; 6 lanes 0.99/0.89/0.71/0.50/0.26), rubbernecking cuts the opposite direction 5-25%; incident mean duration 37 min (82% under 1 h, trucks 63 min); weather: light rain FFS -2 km/h with little capacity effect, heavy rain FFS -5 to -7 and capacity -14 to -15%, heavy snow capacity -30% and FFS -37 to -42 (model as FFS reduction 10 km/h light, 20 heavy rain, 50 heavy snow); darkness -13 to -19%, wet pavement -12 to -18%, weekend -7 to -10%; short-term work zone 1,600 pc/h/ln +/-10% with ca = (1,600 + I - R) fHV N, ramp within 150 m reduces by ramp volume (max half a lane), long-term zones 1,550-2,060 veh/h/ln, lane width below 3.5 m cuts capacity 9-14%; capacity adjustment factor CAF 0.85-1.0 shifts the speed-flow curve at constant density.
does: Scenario builder for run_experiment: applies a named condition (lane blocked, accident, heavy rain, dark, work zone) by changing a road's speed/capacity parameters (e.g. Krauss tau, max speed, lane count) per the HCM factors and tests demand against the reduced capacity first.
outputs: adjusted capacity, whether demand exceeds it, scenario definition
notes: Gives defensible numbers; needs a way to block lanes temporarily in the simulation.

topic: Facility demand from exit counts and boundary checks
idea: Exit demand estimation: time-interval scale factor = sum of entrance demands / sum of exit counts per 15 min (above 1 means congestion hides exit demand), exit demand = exit count x factor; facility spatial limit 15-20 km, boundary cells (first/last interval and first/last segment) must be undersaturated (demand/capacity < 1) or the analysis is flawed; ramp metering evaluated by overriding ramp capacity per interval; analysis proceeds cell by cell, bottleneck cell (D/C > 1) passes capacity, stores unmet demand upstream (shock wave) and transfers it to the next interval via the OD table.
does: Before trusting an experiment, checks that the corridor's boundary segments and first/last 15 minutes are uncongested and estimates hidden demand from counts, and reports the time-space cells where D/C > 1.
outputs: scale factors, boundary violations, bottleneck cells
cite: Ch 22 II, Demand estimation, Demand-Capacity Ratio
notes: Warm-up/cool-down check for simulation runs too (start and end empty).

idea: Oversaturated analysis on nodes and segments with time steps under 15 min: mainline flow MF = min(mainline input, MO1 ramp share, MO2 storage limit (vehicles allowed at queue density), MO3 front-clearing queue after an incident clears, upstream capacity, downstream capacity); queue growth by simplified linear congested flow-density relation and shock wave position; expected demand initialisation as if queues stacked vertically; on-ramp flow = min(input, output), delay and queue at ramps.
does: Fast analytical (cell-transmission-style) forecast of queue length, extent and clearance time upstream of a bottleneck (lane drop, incident, merge) from demand and capacity per interval, used to pre-screen scenarios and check the microscopic run.
inputs: segment capacities, demand by interval, queue density
outputs: queue vehicles per segment, spillback time, clearance time
cite: Ch 22 II Oversaturated Conditions; App A.4
notes: Stdlib cell transmission model; deterministic.

topic: Speed recovery downstream of a slow segment
idea: Maximum achievable speed downstream of a slow segment Vmax = FFS - (FFS - Vprev) e^(-0.0053 L), L the distance between segment midpoints (m); speed with a capacity adjustment factor S = FFS + 1 - exp[(ln(FFS + 1 - 28...)...)] vp keeping density 28 pc/km/ln at the (reduced) capacity; oversaturated time step by shortest segment: 15 s (<=100 m), 25 s (200), 40 s (300), 60 s (>=400 m).
does: Checks that vehicles leaving a queue accelerate back to free-flow speed along the profile Vmax(L) (about 1-2 km), flagging unrealistic recovery in the simulation.
inputs: speed profile downstream of a bottleneck
outputs: observed vs reference recovery distance
cite: Ch 22 App A, Eq A22-1, A22-2, Exhibit A22-4
notes: Companion to capacity_drop_report.

idea: Convert vehicle flow to passenger-car flow: vp = V/(PHF N fHV fp) with fHV = 1/(1 + PT(ET - 1) + PR(ER - 1)); extended segments ET (trucks and buses) 1.5 level, 2.5 rolling, 4.5 mountainous; ER (RVs) 1.2/2.0/4.0; signal approaches ET = 2.0; specific grades by percent grade, length and share of heavy vehicles (equivalents fall as heavy share rises because they platoon); grade of more than 1.0 km below 3% or 0.5 km at 3% or more is its own segment; trucks 75-90 kg/kW weight-to-power, RVs 20-40; driver population factor 0.85 for recreational weekend traffic; freeway speed-flow S = FFS - (23FFS - 1800)/28 x ((vp + 15FFS - 3100)/(20FFS - 1300))^2.6 above vp = 3100 - 15FFS, LOS density 7/11/16/22/28 pc/km/ln, capacity 2,400/2,350/2,300/2,250 pc/h/ln at FFS 120/110/100/90.
does: Makes capacity, v/c and LOS calculations PCU-aware: converts counted flow to pc/h using each vehicle type's stored PCU or the HCM ET by grade, and reports capacity in veh/h for the actual mix.
inputs: flows by vehicle type, PCU, grade
outputs: pc/h/ln, mix-adjusted capacity
existing: none (not_built: PCU in calculations; PCU stored per type)
notes: Directly fills the not-built PCU item.

topic: Weaving segment speed, density and capacity model
idea: Weaving speeds Si = 24 + (SFF + 8 - 24)/(1 + Wi) (24-2, 24-3) with intensity Wi = a (1 + VR)^b (v/N)^c / (3.28 L)^d (24-4), constants by configuration and weaving/nonweaving, constrained or not (Type A unconstrained weaving a 0.15, b 2.2, c 0.97, d 0.80; nonweaving 0.0035, 4.0, 1.3, 0.75; Type B 0.08/2.2/0.70/0.50 and 0.0020/6.0/1.0/0.50; Type C 0.08/2.3/0.80/0.60 and 0.0020/6.0/1.1/0.60); lanes needed by weavers Nw: Type A 1.21 N VR^0.571 L^0.234 / Sw^0.438, B N[0.085 + 0.703 VR + 71.57/L - 0.0112(Snw - Sw)], C N[0.761 + 0.047 VR - 0.00036 L - 0.0031(Snw - Sw)]; constrained when Nw >= Nw(max) (1.4 / 3.5 / 3.0); mean speed S = v/(vw/Sw + vnw/Snw) (24-5); density D = (v/N)/S (24-6); LOS density A <=6, B 12, C 17, D 22, E 27 (multilane 8/15/20/23/25); capacity = flows giving 27 pc/km/ln (25 multilane) found by trial; limits: weaving flow 2,800/4,000/3,500 pc/h for A/B/C, VR 1.0/0.45/0.35/0.20 (type A with 2/3/4/5 lanes), 0.80 B, 0.50 C, R <= 0.40 C, length <= 750 m.
does: Analytic speed, density and LOS of each interchange weaving section (trumpet/diamond ramps) and its capacity limit by iteration, to design ramp spacing and compare with simulated lane-change turbulence.
inputs: weaving and nonweaving flows, length, lanes, configuration, FFS
outputs: Sw, Snw, density, LOS, capacity, constrained flag
notes: Closed form; iterate flows to find capacity.

topic: Ramp junction density and speed model
idea: Merge influence area (450 m, lanes 1-2 plus ramp): v12 = vF PFM with PFM (6-lane) = 0.5775 + 0.000092 LA (adjacent upstream off-ramp: 0.7289 - 0.0000135(vF+vR) - 0.002048 SFR + 0.0002 Lup; adjacent downstream off-ramp: 0.5487 + 0.0801 vD/Ldown; 8-lane 0.2178 - 0.000125 vR + 0.05887 LA/SFR; 4-lane 1.0); equilibrium separation LEQ = 0.0675(vF + vR) + 0.46 LA + 10.24 SFR - 757 (25-2); merge density DR = 3.402 + 0.00456 vR + 0.0048 v12 - 0.01278 LA (25-5); diverge density DR = 2.642 + 0.0053 v12 - 0.0183 LD (25-10); speeds SR = SFF - (SFF - 67) Ms (merge) or Ds (diverge), outer lanes SO = SFF - 0.0058(vOA - 500); LOS by density A <=6, B 12, C 17, D 22, E >22, F when flow exceeds capacity; ramp roadway capacity single lane 2,200 pc/h (FFS >80) down to 1,800 (<30), two-lane 4,400-3,200; a two-lane on-ramp does not raise merge capacity (2,250-2,400 pc/h) without a lane addition.
does: Analytic density, speed and LOS in the influence area of each on/off ramp (v12 prediction, density regression), comparing with the density measured in lanes 1-2 over 450 m in a run and with ramp roadway capacity.
inputs: freeway flow, ramp flow, accel/decel lane length, ramp FFS, lanes
outputs: v12, DR, SR, LOS, ramp capacity check
cite: Ch 25 II, Eq 25-1 to 25-15, Exhibits 25-3 to 25-5
notes: Gives the numeric model behind the earlier ramp check.

idea: Off-ramp flow in lanes 1-2: v12 = vR + (vF - vR) PFD with PFD (6-lane) = 0.760 - 0.000025 vF - 0.000046 vR (adjacent upstream on-ramp 0.717 - 0.000039 vF + 0.184 vU/Lup; adjacent downstream off-ramp 0.616 - 0.000021 vF + 0.038 vD/Ldown), 8-lane 0.436, 4-lane 1.0; two-lane off-ramp PFD 0.450 (6-lane), 0.260 (8-lane); diverge capacities: upstream/downstream freeway 4,800/7,200/9,600 pc/h for 2/3/4 lanes at FFS 120 (2,400 per lane beyond), max flow entering lanes 1-2 = 4,400 pc/h; failure when upstream, downstream freeway or the off-ramp capacity is exceeded; major diverge density D = 0.0109 vF/N over 450 m; left-hand on-ramp v12 times 1.12 (6-lane) or 1.20 (8-lane); fifth-lane flow shares 0.200-0.285 vF; metering gives uniform ramp gaps and lowers breakdown probability.
does: Diverge half of the ramp junction model (flows in lanes 1-2, capacity checks).
inputs: freeway and ramp flows, adjacent ramps
outputs: v12, capacity margin, failure cause
cite: Ch 25 II, Exhibits 25-12 to 25-14, Eq 25-8 to 25-12

topic: Diamond interchange signal offsets and phasing
idea: Signalised diamond: interchange delay dINT = sum(di vi)/sum(vi) over all lane groups and movements including free-flow ramps (26-1), LOS A <=10 ... F >80 s; movement delay = sum of delays of lane groups it passes (e.g. ramp left through = C and B); spacing classes conventional >240 m, compressed 120-240, tight <120; internal-link queue blocking and demand starvation; 3-phase (efficient, internal queue risk; estimate vehicles stored = phase-3 green x ramp left discharge rate vs link storage) vs 4-phase (clear phase per approach, fewer queues, higher delay) vs 4-phase with overlap; offsets: ideal theta = L/S (A26-1), with queue theta = L/S - (1-P) v C / s (A26-2), and to avoid starvation theta >= L/S - 3600 N L/(s l) (A26-3) (l = storage per queued vehicle), use the larger of A26-2 and A26-3 under high volume; avoid spillback onto the freeway (let surface approaches, not exit ramps, fail first); free-flow right turns lower interchange delay (example 37.5 s/veh diamond).
does: For an ACMS diamond or compressed interchange computes inside-link storage, flags 3-phase queue blockage, recommends 3- vs 4-phase with overlap and the offset (A26-1 to A26-3), and reports interchange delay with all movements.
inputs: link length, lanes, ramp left flows, saturation flow, cycle, speed
outputs: storage ratio, phase plan advice, offset, interchange delay
notes: Uses the SPUI/diamond builder geometry; compares with a SPUI via interchange delay.

topic: Bus dwell time and loading-area capacity formulas
idea: Dwell time td = Pa ta + Pb tb + toc (27-2) (alighting and boarding passengers at the busiest door, service times s/p: conventional front door prepaid 2.0, coin 2.6-3.0, alighting 1.7-2.0; two doors 1.2/1.0-1.2; four doors 0.7-0.9; low-floor x0.9, heavy two-way flow x1.2, standees +0.5 s, wheelchair lift 60-200 s (30-60 s ramp), bike rack 20-30 s, door open/close 2-5 s); defaults dwell 60 s CBD, 30 s major outlying, 15 s typical; clearance 10 s (start-up 2-5 + own length 5-10) plus re-entry delay by adjacent lane volume (100 veh/h 0 s, 500 4 s, 1000 14 s); dwell CV typically 0.4-0.8 (0.6); berth capacity Bbb = 3600 (g/C)/(tc + (g/C) td + Za cv td) (27-5), Za one-tail normal for design failure rate (25% 0.675, 10% 1.28, 2.5% 1.96); stop capacity Bs = Neb Bbb (27-6) with linear berth efficiency 100/85/60/20/5%; maximum scheduled load 125-150% of seats (0.4-0.5 m2/p).
does: Gives the simulation an explicit passenger dwell model (boardings and alightings times service time per passenger per door, plus variability) and berth capacity, so bus delay and bunching become realistic and TSP decisions can use dwell prediction.
inputs: boardings, alightings, doors, fare type, bus type, g/C
outputs: dwell time s, berth and stop capacity bus/h
existing: none (not_built: passengers at bus stops, boarding times, loads)
cite: Ch 27 II, Eq 27-2 to 27-6, Exhibits 27-9 to 27-12
notes: Placeholder-level data; institutions' people could drive boardings.

topic: Transit reliability and service LOS thresholds
idea: Headway adherence for routes with 6+ buses/h: cv = standard deviation of headways / scheduled headway (27-1), LOS A 0-0.10, B 0.11-0.20, C 0.21-0.30, D 0.31-0.40, E 0.41-0.50, F >0.50; on-time performance for less frequent routes: late = more than 5 min behind, early departure not on time, LOS A 97.5-100%, B 95-97.4, C 90-94.9, D 85-89.9, E 80-84.9, F <80; frequency LOS by headway A <10 min ... E 30-60, F >60 (buses within 3 min on routes to the same destination count as one); hours of service LOS A >18 h/day ... E 3-11 h; passenger load LOS by m2/p A >1.20, B 0.80-1.20, C 0.60-0.79, D 0.50-0.59, E 0.40-0.49, F <0.40 (load factor 0.5, 0.75, 1.0, 1.25, 1.5 p/seat); amenity thresholds shelter 10/25/50-100 daily boardings.
