does: Adds the LOS grading tables (headway cv, on-time %, frequency, load) to the transit quality report so TSP experiments report whether priority improved reliability grade.
outputs: cv, on-time %, frequency LOS, load LOS

idea: Bus travel speed St = 60/(tr0 + tr1) fs fb (27-14): base running time tr0 by stops per km and dwell (1 stop/km 10 s: 1.39 min/km; 4 stops/km 30 s: 4.16; 8 stops/km 60 s: 12.58), losses tr1 by environment (CBD with right turns 1.5-2.4 min/km, outside CBD 0.4-1.2, mixed traffic 1.8-2.1), skip-stop speed factor fs = 1 - (L1/L2)(v/c)^2(vb/cb), bus-bus interference fb from 1.00 below v/c 0.5 down to 0.69 at 1.0 and 0.35 at 1.2, right-turn capacity factor fr = 1 - fl (vr/cr) with stop-location factors, skip-stop capacity factor fk = (1 + K a (Ns - 1))/Ns with a = 1 - 0.8 (v/c)^3, adjacent lane bus passing factor fp = 1 - 4 Np/3600; acceleration 1.2 m/s2 for stop-to-stop speeds.
does: Predicts bus travel speed and checks the simulated bus run time between stops against it, to detect bus slowdowns from dwell, signals and bus-bus queueing.
inputs: stop spacing, dwell, bus flow, adjacent lane v/c
outputs: expected speed, deviation of simulated speed
cite: Ch 27 II, Eq 27-7 to 27-15, Exhibits 27-18 to 27-21

idea: Six dimensions for a system: quantity of service (person-km PkmT, person-hours PHT, mean trip speed PkmT/PHT), intensity (person-hours of delay, mean delay per person-trip, mean speed), duration (max hours congestion persists anywhere; a segment is congested when demand exceeds discharge capacity), extent (max percent of system km congested at one time), variability (sensitivity: rerun at +/-5% demand and report elasticity = % change in measure / % change in demand; above 1.0 is highly sensitive), accessibility (% of trips or persons reaching a goal within a target time); mean modal delay Dm = sum(Dx Tx + Dp Tp)/sum(Tx + Tp) over segments x and points p weighted by person-trips (28-1); report card matrix by subsystem (freeway, street, transit, pedestrian, bicycle).
does: One tool that turns a run (or an experiment pair) into the six-dimension report card per mode, with the +/-5% demand elasticity and accessibility within a time budget, so the assistant has a standard summary to compare scenarios.
inputs: run_id, vehicle occupancy, demand, optionally +/-5% runs
outputs: PkmT, PHT, person-delay, speed, duration, extent %, elasticity, accessibility
existing: partial: read_results, network_indices, analyse_run (no extent/duration/elasticity/accessibility card)
notes: Congestion defined by demand over capacity, measurable per road as v/c or queue presence.

topic: Default utility function and logit shares
idea: Default multimodal utility U = -0.025 IVT - 0.050 OVT - 0.005 Cost (IVT in-vehicle min, OVT out-of-vehicle min incl. walk and wait, cost in cents) (A28-1) and logit share Pa = e^Ua / sum_j e^Uj (A28-2); out-of-vehicle time weighted twice in-vehicle; utility is relative (preference between options), not an absolute satisfaction, so thresholds must be local.
does: Default coefficients and the 2x out-of-vehicle weighting for choose_modes when no calibrated values exist; compare with the current coefficients.
outputs: utility, mode shares
existing: covered: choose_modes (multinomial logit); coefficients to compare

topic: Corridor demand-capacity adjustment and queue delay
idea: Planning-level corridor model: build a gate tree (segments ranked from an entry gate, highest v/c first, no U-turns); per period excess demand is stored: Queue = Queue(0) + demand - capacity (29-1), downstream demand reduced pro rata until the cut is under 5% of capacity and excess carried to the next hour; queue delay DQ = T Q(h-1)/... + (v - c) T^2/2 (29-4, queue polygon); queue length QL = T (v - c)/(N ds) with storage density ds 75 veh/km/ln freeway (13.3 m spacing), 130 on two-lane/urban (7.5 m) (29-10), overflow if QL exceeds segment length; free-flow and congested traversal times R = L/S; PHT = AVO sum[v R + DQ] (29-5); mean trip time t = 60 PHT/P (29-6); mean speed PkmT/PHT (29-7); mean trip delay d = 3600 (PHT - PHTf)/P (29-8) with free-flow assignment for route diversion delay; duration Hi = Ni T (29-9); first and last periods must be uncongested.
does: Fast (no simulation) corridor forecast of queues, delay, extent and duration per hour for a path set from demand and capacities, used to pre-screen scenarios before runs or to sanity-check run results.
inputs: road capacities, hourly demand per path, AVO
outputs: queue per segment/hour, delay, duration, extent, mean trip speed
notes: Same polygon logic as bottleneck_queue_forecast; this version needs no cell model.

topic: Link volume-delay function calibrated to capacity speed
idea: Areawide link traversal time Rc = Ro + 0.25 T [(X - 1) + sqrt((X-1)^2 + 16 J X L^2 / ... T^2)] (30-5, Akcelik form) + signal zero-flow delay Do = N C/3600 x DF (1 - g/C)^2/2 ... (30-7, DF 0.9 actuated, 1.0 fixed, 1.2/0.9/0.6 coordinated unfavorable/favorable/highly favorable); J chosen so speed at X = 1 matches the detailed method: J = (Rc - Ro)^2/L^2 (30-8), e.g. freeway FFS 120 -> 86 km/h at capacity J 10.9e-6, FFS 100 -> 82: 4.8e-6; arterial class III 3 signals/km FFS 65 -> 28: 200e-6; class IV 6 signals/km 45 -> 7: 7188e-6; link capacity = capacity of its most restrictive point; links split where demand or capacity differs more than 10%; HCM curves replace the BPR curve for congested speeds; BPR alternative in App C; capacity c = Q N fHV fp PHF (30-1) or c = so N fw ... g/C (30-3).
does: A calibrated volume-delay function per road so route choice and assign_routes can use congestion-dependent link times (instead of free-flow or sparse measured times) and critical_links can rank links by predicted delay at the given demand.
inputs: link length, FFS, capacity, signals per km, demand
outputs: predicted traversal time and speed at the demand
existing: partial: assign_routes (shortest routes), critical_links static free flow; not_built: equilibrium assignment
notes: Could also be fit from the simulation's own link times (J from measured speed at capacity).

topic: Calibration and validation protocol for the simulator
idea: Eight-step application: scope, check HCM method, select model, assemble data, input, calibrate and validate, output analysis, alternatives; calibrate on a baseline case with site data (speed, delay, queue length, throughput, density, trajectories), parameters to calibrate (desired speed distribution by driver type, queue discharge headway, lane-change and car-following gaps, vehicle accel/decel); run must start from a realistic initial state, cover the whole analysis period and use time-varying demand within the hour (not an average constant); stochastic results are point estimates so use independent replications with confidence intervals; reuse calibrated parameters for alternatives; use animation to spot anomalies; for design use 85th-95th percentile queue (stochastic microscopic), not mean.
does: A guided checklist the assistant follows before trusting a what-if: baseline vs observed targets (speed, delay, queue, throughput), warm-up and period coverage, replications and CI, and which parameters to tune, recording the result in note_plan.
outputs: calibration report with pass/fail per target and the parameters changed
cite: Ch 31 V Applying a Model, Exhibit 31-17
notes: Pairs with benchmark_physics and required_replications.
